faults.fault_text: The narrowing that fixed fault 27 has made the two pull rules inert on the English a reader actually writes. _pull_against and _stronger_weaker now fire only where a part reference is written out as 'part N' with a digit, and a reader names its parts 'P2', 'P10', '(1)', 'N-bar_I' or by quotation, and writes the verdict under a heading. The gate therefore misses the pulling-pair leak in its commonest real form, which is the shape fault 10 built the gate to catch. The wording that caused it is mine (round 2's forced fix said 'a part reference WRITTEN OUT'), and A1 implemented it exactly; the fault is in the rule as it now stands, not in the fixer's obedience, and A1's dropped list claims 'I found no third form that would catch them without firing on the four innocent lines', which running shows to be wrong.
faults.evidence: Input neither fixer used: the 3,292 lines of the 96 real reports of the record (dry/record96), written by readers under file 33 who knew nothing of this gate. 38 lines state a pull ... against; 18 are missed by the whole gate, and 15 of those 18 open with a pull heading ('**Pull.** P10 (complexity more relevant) pulls against P12 (modesty)', '*Pull:* P2/P5 pull against J3', '- **Pull.** N-bar_I and f_P pull against each other: push N-bar_I up and f_P must fall'). Of all 41 pull/stronger-weaker lines exactly ONE carries 'part N' written out, and the narrowed predicates catch exactly one; the 21 that are caught are caught by the unnarrowed 'pairs? that pull' pattern (14) and by the gives-way/line rule (5). A third form exists and I ran it: PULL_HEADING = r'(?i)^[\s>*_`#-]*(?:\d{1,2}[.)\]][ \t]*)?[\s*_`]*pulls?\b[\s*_`]*[:.–—-]' , plus a label-shaped part reference r'(?i)\bparts?\s+\d{1,2}\b|\bP\s?\d{1,2}\b' beside 'part N'. It raises the catch on the real lines from 21 of 41 to 39 of 41, fires on 0 of fault 27's six innocent lines (including '10. The Crocodile pulls and the Elephant's Child pulls against him.' and '5. The screw pulls the mirror against the casting'), and fires 0 times on the 366 numbered sentences of W1, W9 and W12. It also leaves clean the two innocent lines in that set that open with another heading ('**Change list.** Covers: ... weaker vs stronger reducing class', '- **Direction.** ...').

Add the two forms to partition.py's demo as must-fire lines, keep the innocent seven, and write the remaining give-up into code/README.md (a pull named with neither a heading nor a label -- 'Comprehensiveness pulls against journal word limits' -- is still caught by nothing).
